depth: The depth map lays out a checkout counter directly below and in front of the camera wearer, with a cash register (bottom-right), a tall brown paper bag (centre-left), a jar (far bottom-right), and a red basket (far left) all glowing brightly in the background at roughly 3–5 m away, out of arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person across the counter. Behind the register at roughly 3–5 m stands a person on the upper-right facing away from the camera wearer, positioned about 3–5 m behind the register and distant from the paper bag, while a display case sits nearer on the upper-left at roughly 0.4–1.0 m and within arm's reach. The register and counter edge partially occlude the person's lower body, and in frames 1–4 the upper portion of the person's head is cut off by the top frame boundary before coming partially into view in frame 5 as the camera tilts slightly upward and the person leans slightly backward with both hands moving away from the register drawer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the recessed register cash drawer from its raised keypad housing and highlights the hollow interior depth of the open paper bag and red basket. However, the map looks unreliable in the dark background gap between the person and the paper bag (which collapses to uniform black) and on the flat countertop paper under the bag, which blends smoothly into the bag's base without a sharp depth boundary.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies only a sparse subset of the scene across the five frames: the person standing behind the counter on the upper-right (3–5 m away, facing away from the camera wearer) is segmented in frames 2, 4, and 5, while background objects at 3–5 m (all out of arm's reach of both people) are intermittently segmented beneath misclassified labels. Specifically, the jar on the far right is labelled 'bottle' (frame 1) or 'cup' (frame 5), the cash register in the lower-right is labelled 'laptop' (frame 1) or split into 'keyboard' and 'book' (frame 2), the tall brown paper bag to its left is labelled 'book' across frames 1–4, the cash notes at the bottom-centre are labelled 'cup' (frame 1), and the foreground display case on the upper-left (0.4–1.0 m away and within reach) is labelled 'tv' in frame 5. Across the sequence, the masks reflect the camera tilting slightly upward by frame 5—bringing more of the person's upper torso and neck into the mask while the paper bag on the left drops out of segmentation entirely—and capture the occlusion of the person's lower torso behind the register in frames 2 and 4. While the segmentation map provides sharp outer silhouettes for the person's torso and shoulders against the dark background that are low-contrast in RGB, it is highly unreliable in both class labelling and temporal consistency, completely missing the person in frames 1 and 3 and the red basket on the far left in all frames.
pose: The pose map tracks the skeleton and hands of the single person standing behind the counter on the upper-right (roughly 3–5 m from the camera wearer), who faces directly away from the camera wearer with both hands positioned out of arm's reach of the cash register drawer (3–5 m from the camera wearer) far to the right of the paper bag. In frames 1–4, because the person's head is mostly cropped out at the top edge of the image and the register occludes their waist, the map detects only their raised left hand (magenta) hovering just above the open cash drawer—along with a false-positive miniature yellow body skeleton on the far-right jar in frame 1. Across frames 1 to 4, this left hand shifts slightly downward and leftward relative to the frame as the camera view tilts up, and in frame 5 the full upper-body skeleton (shoulders, torso, both arms, and five facial keypoints at the top edge) appears as the person's head enters the frame and both hands move away from the register drawer about 3–5 m apart. The pose map makes the exact 2D joint articulation of the fingers on the left hand and the symmetric away-facing shoulder alignment in frame 5 much clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, it is unreliable in frames 1–4 where it completely fails to detect the visible torso, arms, and right hand resting on the side of the register, and where it hallucinates a tiny body skeleton on the jar in frame 1.
